newsitem.title: USA: Starbucks plans additional store openings.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks plans additional store openings.

text.p: Starbucks Corp on Thursday said it expects to open at least 231 new stores in continental North America during the remainder of fiscal 1997 and have at least 200 stores in the Pacific Rim by the year 2000.

In a statement accompanying its financial results for the first quarter of fiscal 1997, the coffee chain said the planned North American openings do not include the smaller Breve Bar and Doppio locations.
Starbucks also said it plans to enter the new market of Detroit before the end of fiscal 1997.

For the first quarter ended December 29, Starbucks reported net earnings of $14.4 million or $0.18 a share, up from $9.6 million or $0.13 a share a year ago. Consolidated revenues increased 41 percent to $239.1 million from $169.5 million for the first quarter of fiscal 1996.

Starbucks said retail sales increased 41 percent to $205.3 million, specialty sales revenues increased 51 percent to $25.0 million, and direct response sales increased 22 percent to $8.8 million. Comparable store sales for Starbucks stores increased 3 percent.

During the first fiscal quarter, Starbucks opened 93 new stores and licensees opened five stores in continental North America. Additionally, the first Starbucks stores opened in Honolulu, Hawaii and Singapore during the quarter. There are now 1,102 Starbucks stores in continental North America as well as three in Tokyo, and one each in Hawaii and Singapore.
